The '''High Council Tower''' was a tall spire that housed the [[Jedi Council Chamber/Legends|meeting place]] of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Over the Council's history, the Tower has existed in many different incarnations.<ref name="KOTOR9" /> The most recognizable Tower was located atop the southwestern side of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] surrounding the [[Temple Spire/Legends|Temple Spire]].<ref name="TPM" /> Fully rebuilt circa [[1019 BBY]], the Tower was abandoned in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] and later collapsed during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="ELII">''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand]]''</ref> An exact replica would be constructed for the [[New Jedi Order]] circa [[35 ABY/Legends|35 ABY]].<ref name="FOTJO" />

==History==
===Old Republic===
[[File:Old_Jedi_High_Council_Tower.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Tower as it stood during the [[Mandalorian Wars]].]]

Over the long history of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and their presence on Coruscant, the exact meeting place of the High Council has changed over the many millennia. When the [[Four Masters/Legends|Four Masters]] began building a temple around the [[Sacred spire/Legends|sacred spire]], the Order established a base of operations for the Council in a broad plaza. A narrow tower with a wide base, the Order used this Tower as a store house for [[Sith artifact/Legends|Sith artifacts]] confiscated after the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]. During the [[Mandalorian Wars]], the High Council was notified of a [[Jedi Covenant|schismatic sect]] within the Order. Using this information, the High Council led an attack on the [[Draay Estate]], ground zero for the heretic Jedi, leaving the Tower lightly defended. While the Council was attacking the estate [[Haazen]], the mastermind behind the Covenant, ordered his agents within the Tower to take control of the Sith artifacts stored within. Killing fellow Jedi, the artifacts were secured by the Covenant Jedi; however, Haazen was killed during the battle and the High Council returned to prevent the theft by the misguided Jedi at the Tower.<ref name="KOTORV">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Vindication]]''</ref>

Only a [[3960 BBY|few years later]] the Council had moved to new Council Chamber, located at the base of a tall spire. In [[3954 BBY]] the [[Sith Triumvirate]] revealed itself and began a [[First Jedi Purge|Jedi Purge]], forcing the Order to abandon this Council Tower indefinitely.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> With the reoccupation of Coruscant by the Order, they occupied the Temple as it expanded to greater heights. As of [[3653 BBY]] the Council occupied one of four spires located atop the Temple Ziggurat. However, this tower would collapse during the resurgent [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire's]] [[Sacking of Coruscant|attack]] on the capital.<ref name="Timeline 1" />

[[File:SackingJediTemple-Deceived.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The High Council Tower collapses during the [[Sacking of Coruscant|Sith onslaught]].]]

It wasn't until the expansion of [[1019 BBY]] that the Council and the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] had raised enough money to reconstruct the Tower atop the Temple complex. The Tower would stand for nearly a millennium, with expansions and remodeling of the interior happening every once in a while. In [[34 BBY/Legends|34 BBY]] a group of [[Yinchorri/Legends|Yinchorri]], hired by the mysterious [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], led an [[Raid on the Jedi Temple (Yinchorri Uprising)|attack]] on the Tower. Infiltrating the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|atrium]] of the Tower, the Yinchorri were repelled by the Jedi present in the Temple, causing little damage to the interior of the structure.<ref name="AOW">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Council: Acts of War]]''</ref> Following the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] hangars were constructed in the Council towers, housing new personal [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] for use by individual Jedi.<ref name="SWCL" />

At the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] the Tower served as the headquarters for the Order's war operations, with [[Jedi command/Legends|Jedi Command]] constantly updating the [[Office of the Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Office of the Supreme Chancellor]] and the High Council on [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] movements. At the conclusion of the war, the elusive [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], Darth Sidious, was discovered to be no other than [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] Palpatine of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Known only to the High Council, four of the greatest swords masters of the Order went to arrest the Sith and failed. Though the Temple was on high alert, the small number of fully trained Jedi there was no match for the overwhelming number of the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]. As [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|Operation: Knightfall]] was carried out, the Temple was purged of all its occupants. As the fighting was still going strong, the Council Tower was visited by a concerned [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]], [[Senator/Legends|Galactic Senator]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]]. After being turned away by [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] stationed on the hangar landing platform, Organa watched in horror as [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Zett Jukassa/Legends|Zett Jukassa]] was slaughtered by the troops.<ref name="ROTS" />

[[File:Ruinsoftowers.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Tower, as viewed by [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]] from the [[Tower of First Knowledge/Legends|Tower of First Knowledge]].]]

Following the disbanding of the Order, the Tower would stand in silence, its halls abandoned and its superstructure crumbling. Though illegal to enter and strictly guarded by [[Imperial Senate Sentinel]]s ex-Jedi [[Ferus Olin]] managed to force his way through a boarded-up [[Jedi Temple refectory/Legends|breakfast room]] window and make it to the base of the Tower. Olin met Darth Vader here in the atrium and proceeded to [[Duel in the Jedi Temple (Ferus Olin)|duel]] the Sith Lord as they made their way to the Council Chambers. Olin managed to escape the Sith's wrath by dropping through a hole in the floor, landing in the [[High Council holomap room/Legends|map room]] several stories below.<ref name="LJR" />

In [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], during the [[Sith assassin/Legends|Sith assassin]] [[Galen Marek|Starkiller's]] [[Starkiller's Trial of the Spirit|third mission]] to the Temple, the assassin entered into a chamber at the base of the Tower with a turbolift lobby. Taking the lift to the summit of the Tower he proceeded into the ruined chamber after cutting his way through countless [[Shadow stormtrooper/Legends|Shadow Troopers]]. The malfunctioning [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]] program activated as Starkiller entered the room, using the Council Chamber's holoprojectors to create a simulacrum of dead Jedi named [[Kento Marek]]. Battling the simulated Jedi, Starkiller defeated the simulacrum and left the chamber in increased distress.<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> Elements of the design for the High Council Tower were later incorporated into the [[Emperor's Tower/Legends|Emperor's Tower]] on the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]], though unlike the actual High Council Tower where it was only one of five spires of the Jedi Temple, the Emperor's Tower only had one spire, symbolic to how Palpatine was in total control of the Empire and didn't need to answer to a council.<ref name="S&V 9">[[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 9|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 9]]</ref>

The Temple would survive for much of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Council Tower leering over the surface of Coruscant for years. The ancient edifice was even re-inhabited briefly, as members of the [[new Jedi Order]] searched the destroyed hall for any information on the teachings of the old Order.<ref name="BRS">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]''</ref> It wasn't until several years later that the five towers of the Temple collapsed, the Council Tower completely destroyed. The new Order would clear the rubble away and erect a [[Jedi Headquarters|small praxeum]] in its place on the roof of the Ziggurat;<ref name="Star Wars: Union">''[[Star Wars: Union]]''</ref> though this too would be lost during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="ELII" />

===Reconstruction===
[[File:NewTempleOnCoruscant.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Tower is rebuilt in the [[new Jedi Temple]]; though it is concealed behind the tinted [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]] pyramid.]]
Following the retaking of Coruscant by the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]], [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Cal Omas]] donated a [[New Jedi Temple|new Temple]] to the Order in recognition of the Jedi's efforts during the war. Using blueprints salvaged from the old [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]] the [[Reconstruction Authority]] erected the new Temple to near-exact specifications; though a new [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]] pyramid concealed the restored Council Tower. In [[43 ABY]], Interim Grand Master [[Kenth Hamner]] reflected on this architectural choice and wondered why those who built the Temple couldn't stay with a design that had worked for centuries.<ref name="FOTJO" />

==Layout==
The ancient Tower that housed the chambers of the High Council stood the test of time over the Order's long history, standing high Over Coruscant for nearly a century. The masonry of the spire was supported by a highly-tensile substance known as [[Magnite/Legends|magnite]], which aided in the support of the thin frame of the Tower. Also, the permem incorporated into the Council Chamber's windows aided in maintaining a constant gravity balance, along with keeping the artificial air supply operational at such altitude. The [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolift]] that led to the Council Chamber was crafted by great Jedi architects, who incorporated Force-inspired, internal dynamics, which allowed for the different sizes and shapes of the Order's members to ascend the narrow spire.<ref name="SWCL" />

[[File:Jedi_Council_Tower_balcony.png|thumb|left|250px|Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his Padawan, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], make use of a Contemplation Station.]]
Crowning each of the Temple spires were reception/transmission antennas which, along with a constant connection to the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]], tapped into the cosmic energy fields of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] itself in order to stay in contact with Jedi on far-flung planets. The central topmast of this unique array was a powerful multi-frequency [[Eradicator (communications scrambler)|eradicator]]/scrambler that when coupled with the eradicators incorporated into the Tower's frame scrambled all communications in and out of the Temple. Communication bundles in the wall cavities fed data from these masts, through the columns within the Council Chamber, to the [[High Council holomap room|Operations Planning Center]]. Receiver vanes within the walls of the spire converted signals from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] locations into real-space coordinates before displaying them on the holomap in the central pit of the Planning Center. From here, the location of Jedi stationed anywhere in the galaxy could be pinpointed, and disturbances in the Force or high concentrations of Force energy were displayed on the map by [[Jedi command/Legends|Jedi Command]]. The Operations Planning Center gave access to the three Contemplation Stations outside<ref name="SWCL" />

At the base of each Tower was a [[Jedi Temple/Legends|reception hall]] that allowed rooftop access to and from the Temple. Two large bronzium statues flanked the entrance; their lightsabers crossed over the entry. The hall beyond was lined with statues of the great Jedi Masters of old, leading to a bridge that spanned the central shaft that ran up the Tower; suspended in the shaft was a large stone statue of a Jedi.<ref name="TFU" /> An ancient stairway wound around the shaft, leading up into the heights of the Tower, all the way to the High Council Chamber.<ref name="LJR" />

[[File:ITW1_Council_Chamber.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Cutaway of the High Council Tower]]
Fifteen stories below the Council Chamber was a hangar equipped with garages below the floor and an aircraft control station in the ceiling. A retractable landing platform could be extended from the chamber's mouth out over the Temple Ziggurat for easy launches from the hangar.<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> The room was staffed by [[Temple employee|mechanics]] and [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]], as well as clone personnel during the Clone Wars.<ref name="ROTS" />

The residences of the High Council members were also located in the Tower, providing them were more private accommodations and immediate access to the Council Chamber. Located above the atrium to the Tower, the chambers were typically small and hexagonal, with meditation cushions placed in the center of the room.<ref name="AOTC" /> Following the reconstruction of the Tower in [[35 ABY/Legends|35 ABY]], the [[Grand Master's offices]] were completed with a white [[larmalstone]] foyer. These offices were located below the [[Situation Room/Legends|Situation Room]] and above the quarters of the other Jedi Council members.<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Betrayal">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
An inconsistency exists in some appearances of the Tower, specifically the Council Chamber. In some shots an antechamber lies beyond the doors to the chamber; which does not comply with the tower's cylindrical shape.
